target_c3_positive.large_positive_probe_execution_change: At larger positive probes the raw corrector changes from the center's 1 accepted substep / 0 retry / 0 temporal rejection route to 2 accepted substeps / 1 retry / 1 temporal rejection.
target_c3_positive.interpretation: G09's >5% half-step mismatch at C3 positive is caused by a finite-difference stencil crossing a temporal-execution topology change, not by participant inadmissibility.

control_c2_negative.interpretation: The C2-negative neighborhood has deterministic fragmented numerical admissibility; status-6 points fail in the raw corrector with result_status 2 and repeated solver rejections, while available negative-side probes matching the center execution topology provide a stable slope.

bounded_conclusions: G09 must remain falsified; G09A diagnoses rather than repairs it.

Participant status alone is insufficient to decide whether a probe represents the local derivative: C3-positive probes can all be status 0 yet cross an execution-topology boundary and distort the finite-difference slope.
The C2-negative status fragmentation is numerical/component-domain behavior, supported by raw solver-rejection signatures, not evidence of a discontinuous physical hydrological q(H).
A defensible next estimator should filter derivative probes by equality of accepted execution topology with the current center state before central or one-sided differencing.
No production change or admission follows from G09A.
